title: Neuro Exam Decision Tree
description: Case-based MicroSim in which students run neurological exam steps and imaging on three fictional patients (a left-hemisphere stroke pattern, a peripheral facial nerve palsy, and a thoracic spinal cord lesion), collect findings, and localize the lesion, with feedback explaining the reasoning.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: Neuroscience
learningObjectives: Localize a lesion to the left or right cerebral hemisphere, brainstem, spinal cord, peripheral nerve, or muscle from a pattern of exam findings
Distinguish upper motor neuron signs (brisk reflexes, Babinski sign, spasticity) from lower motor neuron signs
Explain why forehead-sparing facial weakness points to the brain while whole-face weakness points to the facial nerve
Recognize a sensory level as a sign of spinal cord disease
prerequisites: Chapter 4: major brain regions and cranial nerves
Chapter 7: the corticospinal tract crosses to the opposite side; reflex arcs
Chapter 14: stroke and the middle cerebral artery
keyQuestions: Is the problem in the central nervous system (upper motor neuron) or the peripheral nervous system (lower motor neuron)?
Which side of the nervous system is involved, given that motor pathways cross?
At what level is the problem: cortex, brainstem, spinal cord, nerve, or muscle?
Which exam steps give the most information for each case?
misconceptions: A stroke in the left hemisphere weakens the left side of the body
Any one-sided facial droop is a stroke
A brain scan alone can locate every neurological problem, so the exam is unnecessary
A head CT can show the spinal cord in the chest region
controls: Nine exam-step buttons: Mental status, Cranial nerves, Strength, Reflexes, Sensation, Coordination, Gait, Order CT, Order MRI
Location select menu (6 choices) and Check button
assumptions: Cases are fictional composites with classic, textbook findings
At least 3 exam steps are required before checking a localization
After two wrong attempts the correct location is revealed
limitations: Real patients often show incomplete or mixed findings
The sim localizes lesions but does not teach treatment decisions
Imaging results are described in words, not shown as images
accessibility: describe() screen-reader summary; native keyboard-accessible buttons and menus; feedback uses both color and text labels
